Standard: A zipper has two chains with teeth, and a slider that joins them. When the slider is at one end (stop A), the chains are unjoined from A to B (the whole thing open). When the slider moves toward B, it joins the chains behind it. When the slider reaches B, the whole thing is joined (closed). So the closed portion is behind the slider (on the side of the last stopper it passed), and the open portion is ahead (toward the stopper it's heading to).

So if the slider is currently at stop A (fully open), the open portion is the whole loop ahead, and to close we move it toward B. If the slider is somewhere in the middle, the closed portion is behind (from A to slider) and open ahead (slider to B).
